facts.text: Grad B said the reasons the initial (flat) design was unsatisfying were that it would be a pain to set up all the necessary probabilities, and that moving to learning of some sort would leave them handicapped, since Grad B does not know belief-nets well.
facts.source_quote: Reasons being , you know , it 'd be a pain to set up all the probabilities for that . If we moved onto the next step and did learning of some sort , uh according Bhaskara we 'd be handicapped .

facts.text: Grad C noted that with N features all pointing to one node, the number of probability parameters needed is exponential in N (two to the N).
facts.source_quote: Well usually , I mean , you know , N {disfmarker} If you have N features , then it 's two to the N {disfmarker} {pause} or exponential in N .

facts.text: In the team's initial (flat) design, all the features pointed directly to a single node.
facts.source_quote: Yeah , they 'd all be like pointing to the one node .

facts.text: Grad B said the team's next idea, in response to these problems, was to add a middle layer to the belief net.
facts.source_quote: So then our next idea was to add a middle layer , right ?

facts.text: Grad B explained the rationale for the middle layer: the person at the screen is trying to communicate an abstract idea (e.g., "I am a tourist, I want to go to this place"), drawn from features of the communication.

"

facts.text: Grad B said the hidden (middle-layer) variables the team came up with were whether the person was on a tour, running an errand, or in a hurry.
facts.source_quote: the hidden variables {disfmarker} hair variables we came up with were whether someone was on a tour , running an errand , or whether they were in a hurry

facts.text: The team reasoned that someone in a hurry would be less likely to want to do 'Vista' (view/sightsee), since wanting to view things implies not being in a hurry.
facts.source_quote: right ? Because {pause} if you want to view things you wouldn't be in a hurry .

facts.text: Grad B said someone in a hurry might instead be more likely to be using their stated destination as a navigational point en route to another place, rather than as a final destination.
facts.source_quote: Or they might be more likely to be using the place that they want to go to as a {disfmarker} like a {pause} navigational point to go to another place .

facts.text: Grad B said other hidden/middle-layer variables the team considered were whether the destination was the person's final destination, and whether the destination was closed.
facts.source_quote: Whether the destination was their final destination , whether the destination was closed .

facts.text: Grad B said the belief-net was still in a 'toy' version at this point, because the team did not yet know what probabilities to assign.

relations.text: The team added a middle layer specifically because the flat, all-features-to-one-node structure was too costly to parameterize (probabilities hard to set up, exponential in the number of features) and would not scale to future learning.
